fixes.old: Walking alone has the widest WHO window, from 8.2 to 17.6 months.
fixes.new: Walking alone has the latest WHO window, from 8.2 to 17.6 months.
fixes.why: Not the widest. Walking alone spans 9.4 months (8.2 to 17.6), standing alone spans 10.0 months (6.9 to 16.9) in the WHO Motor Development Study.

fixes.old: 1 to 2 years: first steps can come anywhere from 8 to 18 months
fixes.new: 1 to 2 years: most first steps come between 8 and 18 months
fixes.why: Overclaim. The WHO window covers 98 in 100 children (1st to 99th percentile), and healthy children in the Zurich study walked as late as 20 months. 'Anywhere from' implies a hard limit.

fixes.old: • Milestones are windows. Walking alone ranges from 8.2 to 17.6 months in WHO data.
fixes.new: • Milestones are windows. Walking alone ranges from 8.2 to 17.6 months for 98 in 100 children in WHO data.
fixes.why: The window is the 1st to 99th percentile, not the full range (WHO Motor Development Study 2006). Keeps the summary consistent with the body.

fixes.old: Crawling is not on the CDC checklists at any age. There are no age-based norms for it, and 4.3% of babies
fixes.new: Crawling is not on the CDC checklists at any age. The CDC dropped it largely for lack of data, and 4.3% of babies
fixes.why: 'No age-based norms' contradicts the WHO crawling window (5.2 to 13.5 months) in the table above. Geil (The Conversation, via Healthed, 29 September 2023) says the CDC reasoning centred on data, and that there are no normative charts like those for walking, which is a narrower claim.
The CDC 3-year item is 'Asks who, what, where, or why questions'. Any 1 type counts, the original implied both were needed.

Verified with no change: WHO windows, 816 children, 5 countries, 1st to 99th percentile, 4.3% never crawled (WHO MGRS Group, Acta Paediatrica 2006). Mott Poll (released 28 June 2021, fielded January 2021, 779 parents of children 0 to 5): 38% sibling, 34% friend's children, 58% vs 27% worried vs not worried. Zurich: 222 children, 8.5 to 20 months, mean 12 months. CDC 2022 at 75% or more, first revision since 2004, previous lists about the 50th percentile (HealthDay, PolitiFact), 'told to wait' finding (Zubler and colleagues, Pediatrics 2022). All CDC items quoted at 2, 4, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 24, 30 months and 3, 4, 5 years. AAP walker claims and 15 August 2022 date. NHS reviews, sentence age, bilingual and self-referral text. Healthier Together bottom shuffling and movement flags. NIJZ whole-child principle.

Loss of skills is correctly attributed to the CDC ('has lost skills he or she once had ... act early'). The Healthier Together page does not itself list general loss of skills, only walking that suddenly becomes unsteady, and the article attributes it correctly.
Consider adding a line that any worry about hearing is worth raising with a GP or health visitor. Not added because I did not find a single NHS page wording that fits cleanly.

The jerking or twitching flag can indicate seizures such as infantile spasms, which need same-day medical review. The Healthier Together page only says to speak to a health visitor or GP. The editor may want a separate, sourced urgent-care line.

NHS self-referral to speech and language therapy: the NHS page says 'you can refer your child to a speech and language therapist yourself', but availability varies by area and nation. 'In the UK' is slightly broad, 'In many areas' would be safer.
Mumsnet links return 403 to automated fetches (Cloudflare) but the threads exist and match the article's descriptions.
